fictionLines.text: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Ines Duarte is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
"Ines's gone." Jacob looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Ines." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Paolo blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
📖 The Codex turns a page: Ines Duarte, 42 days. The mantle passes to Paolo Schmid.
🪞 You wake up somebody else. Paolo Schmid, 38 — a barber.
The village's quarrel was with Ines — and Ines is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
At the grave, Jacob, Everett, Nino and 1 more speak for Paolo — "Ines trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
The fire knew Paolo before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

convoLines.text: "Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Still on what you dream about. That's my read."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Drum-Belly? Paolo is pushing 'The Ugly Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part."
"What if it's art? Like — the whole thing. We're not an experiment, we're a medium. It's sculpting us."
"Take your time."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with June. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that. Doesn't matter now."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"...Anyway. Sorry. What's on your mind?"
"I dreamed Senan was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
Everett has an edge today — something curdled.
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that. Not that it matters."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask?"
"Senan always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should get back to it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen. How are you holding up, though?"
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? That's my read."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Hushpuppy? Paolo is pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I write everything down instead."
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Simone about the pantry run — Simone's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the north treeline by the fallen oak and we'll fill packs before dark."

"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
